newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary grains futures surge in brisk trade.
newsitem.headline: Hungary grains futures surge in brisk trade.

text.p: Grains futures trade on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) revved up on Friday to produce two-thirds of the turnover of the previous four days combined, with nearly all prices rising sharply, the BCE said.
Traders said international price rises prompted them to abandon the wait-and-see attitude that had predominated for much of the week.
"Rising Chicago prices were the main factor behind today's price rises," said Gabor Gyori of Order.
Milling wheat prices rose by the daily 400 forints limit for all maturities except August and September, which gained 250 and 350 forints per tonne respectively to end at 21,650 and 22,260 forints.
Milling wheat accounted for 1,251 of the total turnover of 1,551 contracts, or 680 million forints.
Feed barley prices followed milling wheat, with the nearer positions rising particularly sharply.
July barley closed at 18,500 forints, up 400, September put on 290 to end at 18,850 and December finished unchanged at 19,500 forints.
The increase of maize prices was mainly restricted to the 1996 crop with May ending at 18,100 forints, up 380, and July finishing at 17,700, up 190.
Gyori said speculation in those two maturities was probably the strongest with a large number of open contracts -- 3,691 for May and 5,320 for July.
He said speculators would have to start closing their May positions shortly.
Gyori was unsure about the general market trend next week, but said he did not expect a downward movement.
"I don't think prices can or will go lower," Gyori said.
